what: Letting go of the unread values of every durable row at a build's end (every function, not only `lru` ones; sound through the `keep` path) freed 110 MiB of live heap and not one MB of resident memory, and made each build's end 15 ms longer (`unread values` 1.1 ms to 16.4 ms median, a walk of 2.3 million rows). Built, measured, taken out.
cause: freed blocks share mimalloc pages with live ones, so nothing goes back (docs/memory-footprint.md says so of codegen; it holds for query values too); the query storage line in serve.log counts live bytes, which is not what the daemon weighs
workaround: only whole arrays, regions and pool pages can go back; values have to be records in pool pages to count
state: recorded in restore.md; the patch is /tmp/records-1111/tried-durable-value-eviction.patch on the Mac
